title: How She Built a 6-Figure Business Teaching People About Goats

stated_problem.quote: I wanna keep doing this 'cause I love doing it. How do I make money doing it?
stated_problem.speaker: Deborah

idea.name: Online goat-raising courses
idea.one_liner: Sell detailed online courses that help goat owners care for their herds, with follow-up answers to questions.
idea.customer: Goat owners and people considering raising goats.
idea.offer: Recorded courses on goat health, nutrition, parasites and other goat-raising topics, with question sections for herd-specific follow-up.
idea.revenue_model: One-time course purchases; current course prices are not clearly stated.

key_quotes.quote: It launched in early 2017 and we had a few hundred people buy it, but then I immediately started working on the individual courses
So if you watch this video and you still have questions then you post in the comments section and I'll respond and answer your question that is very specific to your herd.

claims.claim: The first course launched in early 2017 and sold to a few hundred people.
claims.quote: It launched in early 2017 and we had a few hundred people buy it

claims.claim: The email list had 2,000 people when the course launched.
claims.quote: I had 2,000 people on the email list.

claims.claim: The host characterized the launch conversion rate as 10%; Deborah said it was her highest conversion rate.
claims.quote: But 10% of them bought, like that's a huge conversion rate.

claims.claim: Deborah confirmed it was her highest conversion rate.
claims.quote: And that's like the highest my conversion rate ever was.

claims.claim: About 75% of buyers purchased as soon as the cart opened.
claims.quote: probably 75% of people bought as soon as the card opened because I think it was 'cause I had them so hyped up.

claims.claim: The host described $97 as a course price; Deborah did not confirm it in this exchange.
claims.quote: I'm gonna cannibalize my course business by offering this lower price membership?

claims.claim: The host posed charging $50, $100, or $200 or more for a course as a hypothetical comparison.
claims.quote: now I want to charge 50, 100, 200 or more for an online course with the same material

claims.claim: Courses and membership together accounted for 70% of income.
claims.quote: 70% of the income is from the courses in membership.

claims.claim: The host reported that the business owner spent about 40 to 50 hours a week at her desk.
claims.quote: Right now, it usually means me at my desk for about 40 to 50 hours a week

acquisition_channels.details: Built an email list, kept subscribers updated during course creation, and launched to that audience.
Website articles, YouTube videos and podcast content draw goat owners into the business.

ideas.delivery: Recorded online lessons with a comments section for herd-specific questions; Deborah or her team responds. Courses are hosted with the community on Mighty Networks.

prices: $50/$100/$200+ course prices were posed hypothetically by the host
$97 course price was mentioned by the host but not confirmed

ideas.other_uk_rules: For UK sales, consider consumer rights for digital content and UK GDPR/PECR requirements for email-list marketing.

idea.customer: Readers interested in homesteading and raising goats.
idea.offer: Books on homesteading and goat care, published through a traditional publisher.
idea.revenue_model: Publisher advance and royalties on book sales.

The royalty was 10% of wholesale, which was $1 per book.

claims.claim: All her books had sold around 25,000 copies by the time of the interview.
claims.quote: If I add up all of my books together, they sold around 25,000 copies so far.

claims.claim: The first print run of one book was 5,000 copies and sold out in about nine months.
claims.quote: the first print run was 5,000 copies and it sold out within about nine months

claims.claim: The book's stated price was $20 and royalty was 10% of wholesale, or $1 per book.
claims.quote: in 2011 when that book was published, it was $20. And the royalty was 10% of wholesale, which was $1 per book.

claims.claim: The advance was $3,000.
claims.quote: My advance was $3,000.

idea.name: Goat-owner paid membership
idea.one_liner: Charge goat owners a recurring fee for a private community, course access and live expert support.
idea.customer: Goat owners who want ongoing advice tailored to their herd and farm.
idea.offer: Private community, access to goat courses, question support and premium Zoom calls.

key_quotes.quote: That is what makes the membership so valuable to people is because you can read this stuff all day long.
So if somebody has a question, we answer their question, because it is unique to them.

claims.claim: The host described the membership price as $19 to $29 per month.
claims.quote: Today, priced at $19 to $29 per month.

claims.claim: Twenty people joined when the membership launched in 2019.
claims.quote: when I first launched it in 2019, we had 20 people join.

claims.claim: The membership had grown to 150 members.
claims.quote: And every year, we're up to 150 members now.

claims.claim: The early membership had two meetings a month, usually with two or three attendees, lasting about an hour.
claims.quote: we would usually have two or three people in our Zoom meetings. And we only had two meetings a month, and they would only last about an hour.

claims.claim: The membership had three calls a month, lasting about one and a half to two hours each.
claims.quote: We are now up to three calls a month and they probably last an hour and a half to two hours

claims.claim: Two thirds of members joined at the premium level for the Zoom calls.
claims.quote: two thirds of people do join at the premium level because they want the Zoom calls.

claims.claim: The host referred to a $287 annual price while asking about the included farm event; Deborah confirmed the event was included, not the price.
claims.quote: And you're included that at the $287 a year or they paid like extra to come to the farm?

claims.claim: Courses and membership together accounted for 70% of income.
claims.quote: 70% of the income is from the courses in membership.

acquisition_channels.details: Promoted the membership to the existing email list.
Website, YouTube and podcast content drew goat owners into the business.
The private member community and referrals from members support enrollment.

ideas.delivery: Members use a private Mighty Networks community with course access; premium members also receive live Zoom calls. Deborah and experienced team members answer questions.
ideas.other_uk_rules: For UK subscriptions, consider consumer cancellation and renewal requirements, including the DMCC Act subscription regime if applicable; use UK GDPR/PECR compliant email marketing.

idea.name: Niche goat-care website with display ads
idea.one_liner: Publish free goat-care articles and earn advertising income from readers.
idea.customer: Goat owners searching for practical care information; advertisers reach that audience.
idea.offer: A library of goat-care articles with display ads and embedded video advertising.
idea.revenue_model: Display-ad revenue and video ad revenue on the website.

key_quotes.quote: So for all those people who just want free information, if you are reading articles on my website, we are making a few pennies off of you reading that because we're gonna see ads.
we had uploaded maybe 20 videos on Mediavine, and we quit because we were not even making a dollar a month on those videos

claims.claim: Website display ads generated 25% of income.
claims.quote: 25% of the income is from ads on my website.

claims.claim: Website advertising income had reached $3,000 a month, fell to a little over $1,000, and later recovered to a couple thousand dollars a month.
claims.quote: We had been all the way up to $3,000 a month on income with the ads, and it got all the way down to like a thousand something, but it was a very gradual decline and now we're back up to a couple thousand dollars a month

claims.claim: The site had around 700 articles.
claims.quote: In our website, we have over 700 articles on our website now.

claims.claim: Website visits fell from 110,000 to 40,000 per month and later rebounded to about 60,000 per month.
claims.quote: So almost overnight, I went from 110,000 visits per month to 40,000 visits per month.

claims.claim: The host said 25% of income came from website ads.
claims.quote: 25% of the income is from ads on my website.

claims.claim: Videos moved to Reactive had earned over $100 in the first month.
claims.quote: Just with the videos that got moved over to reactive, we had made like over $100 in the first month

claims.claim: On Mediavine, roughly 20 videos earned less than a dollar a month, according to Deborah.
claims.quote: we had uploaded maybe 20 videos on Mediavine, and we quit because we were not even making a dollar a month on those videos

claims.claim: The website video ads paid more than YouTube embeds, though the amount was not specified.
claims.quote: We get paid a lot more for people watching our videos on our website than when we were just embedding YouTube videos

acquisition_channels.details: Articles answer common goat-care search queries.
Website articles connect readers to the email list, YouTube videos and podcast.

ideas.delivery: Readers access articles on the website; ad networks place display and video ads. Deborah's team uploads video assets to the ad platform.

prices: a couple thousand dollars/month after recovery
over $100 in first month from videos on Reactive

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR/PECR rules may apply to advertising cookies and tracking technologies on the site.
